entries.normative_statement: Craft Method specializes Method as a recursive construction chain that preserves typed identity, canonical source authority, separate construction and conformance, generated-view derivation, typed residue, child-to-parent recomposition, and owner-controlled closure. Its ledger preserves continuity but is not the Method itself.

A Method is a governed repeatable transformation whose scope, inputs, actions, roles, gates, outputs, evidence, residue rule, validation rule, recomposition rule, and boundary are explicit. A named Method specializes this form without inheriting authority to execute.

A Goal states a desired future outcome for one Project and becomes achieved only when all required success conditions have adequate evidence and the Goal owner records the lifecycle transition. Progress or passing checks alone do not achieve it.

A Project is a durable coordination identity with purpose, scope, exclusions, owner routes, Goal references, evidence index, purpose or Product connections, lifecycle, and challenge route. Its identity survives changes to plans, tasks, folders, tools, and implementations.

A Workflow is an ordered multi-step orchestration of Operations within or across Product Feature boundaries. It declares exactly one scope from intra-feature or cross-feature and one ownership-boundary scope. Workflow evaluation may emit recovery intent and a plan, but only a separate executor may invoke exact Operation bindings.

An Actor is a governed participant identity to which participation in Lab activity can be attributed. Actor classification establishes neither agency, personhood, capability, ownership, Role, permission, nor authority.

An Admission Transaction is a closed, all-or-nothing application record for one exact authorized Decision Bundle. It verifies the bundle digest, each Decision core digest, authorization evidence, input Project State, and every exact admission target before mutation; then it applies all declared effects and their deterministic receipts, event appends, indexes, projections, and Project State successor as one recoverable unit. It creates no authority beyond the selected outcomes of its member Decisions.

An Agent is an Actor that operates within an explicit Session, Context, Assignment, Policy, and authority boundary to perform attributable Actions with declared Capabilities and Tools. Capability does not grant authority, and Agent output is not automatically fact, decision, admission, Project State, or external effect.

An Agent Action is an immutable attributable record of one proposed, attempted, completed, rejected, or failed operation by an Agent Instance within one Session. The Action record does not prove that its claimed output, delivery, or external effect occurred.

An Agent Assignment is a time-bounded owner-qualified binding of an Agent to an Intent, Goal, Project, Work item, Run, Role, or Responsibility. Assignment establishes expected participation and scope but grants no authority without an exact Authority Claim or Delegation.

An Agent Capability is a bounded class of action or interpretation that an Agent may be technically able to attempt under exact input, output, evidence, and failure contracts. Agent Capability is distinct from Product Capability, Tool, Implementation, Role, authority, and successful performance.

An Agent Instance is one time-bounded concrete realization of Agent, bound to a Profile, Implementation, capability set, accountable Principal, owner route, and lifecycle. It is not a Person, model, Implementation, Session, or authority grant; a Machine Agent Instance cannot outlive or span Sessions.

An Agent Profile is a reusable versioned contract for allowed inputs, outputs, behavior, Policies, Context, tool classes, evidence, escalation, and stop conditions. A Profile is neither an active Agent Instance, Session, capability grant, Implementation, model, nor authority grant.

An Agent Reflection is an attributable revisable diagnostic interpretation of exact Agent Sessions, Actions, outputs, observations, feedback, evidence, and residue. It is not hidden chain of thought, Observation, Finding, Decision, Definition, Policy, proof of improvement, or authority.

An Agent Session is a bounded execution context binding one Agent Instance to one Assignment, Context View, Ontology View, Policy set, authority envelope, inputs, budgets, cursor, Session Memory, and termination state. A Session is neither durable Agent identity nor Project State; terminating a Machine Agent Session also terminates its Machine Agent Instance.

Append-Only Event Ledger is the normalized architecture-pattern identified by semantic.append-only-event-ledger-pattern, owned within scope.repository-governance, and carried by type.architecture-pattern. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D26 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

Append-only event ledger is a CyberAlchemy v2 ledger pattern for state-changing
or authority-affecting operations where each change is recorded as an additive
event instead of silently rewriting prior state.

An append-only event ledger must preserve:

- registered event kinds or event catalog membership
- deterministic subject or stream identity
- idempotency key or duplicate-guard rule for retryable operations
- event payload or source reference
- actor, owner, or route
- timestamp or ordering handle
- replay, projection, or human-audit interpretation

Artifact is the normalized definition identified by semantic.artifact, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.definition. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D51 without silently merging it with another target.

Target-specific normative meaning:

An Artifact is an identity-bearing, typed, versioned record produced or maintained for a declared purpose whose canonical machine representation, generated human projection, ownership, provenance, lifecycle posture, and validation surface are explicit.

Bound source-semantic basis:

A canonical artifact is an artifact instance whose **kind is a member of the
canonical-kind enumeration** ([../../ontology/canonical-kinds/CANONICAL-KINDS.md](../../ontology/canonical-kinds/CANONICAL-KINDS.md))
and whose responsible owner has admitted an exact `process_origin` declaration
that names one allowed producer and process for that kind. It therefore carries
a defined type (a `CAV2-D21` classification/schema facet that is bound, not left
as residue) and an owner-declared process origin.

The strength of support for the origin declaration is recorded separately as
`origin_assurance`:

- `declared` means an owner or source made the exact origin statement;
- `integrity-bound` means a verifier confirmed that the statement and bound
  artifact-state bytes match an L1 integrity mechanism; and
- `actor-attested` means an identified actor attested the exact tuple under a
  bound L2 identity policy and external signature.

`actor-attested` is a defined future level, not a currently available result.
No assurance level proves that the named process actually executed, that the
statement is true, or that the artifact is correct or authoritative.

Canonical-ness is therefore the property of *being typed and carrying an
owner-admitted, allowed process-origin declaration with an honest assurance
level*. It is **decoupled from authority** — a canonical artifact may be
non-authoritative and still canonical. An artifact whose kind is not in the
enumeration, or whose exact origin does not resolve to an owner-approved producer
for that kind, is non-canonical or remains blocked as typed residue.

Artifact Lifetime is the normalized definition identified by semantic.artifact-lifetime, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.definition. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D52 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

Artifact durability is the axis that classifies a `CAV2-D51` canonical artifact by
**intended lifespan** — `ephemeral` (a work-product meant to be produced,
consumed, and retired) or `perennial` (a standing reference meant to endure and be
maintained). Durability is **orthogonal** to the `authority_kind` (`CAV2-D49`)
and to maturity/status (`CAV2-D23`): two artifacts of the same kind may differ in
durability — a discovery and an inventory index are both `Evidence`, yet the
discovery is ephemeral and the index is perennial.

Durability carries one **contradiction-tolerance** obligation (typed coupling,
`CAV2-D16`):

- an **ephemeral** artifact **may hold live contradictions** — competing
  hypotheses and unresolved tensions are expected and preserved;
- a **perennial** artifact **must not hold live simultaneous contradictions**.
  *Temporal supersession* — a later entry overriding an earlier one in an
  append-only record (`CAV2-D26` ledger), or a decision record narrating the
  contradiction it resolved (`CAV2-D36`) — is **not** a live contradiction and is
  permitted.

Every governed file f in package P has exactly one declared surface role from canonical-instance, declared-component, generated-projection, evidence, fixture, or transient-state. A canonical instance resolves to exactly one admitted Artifact Type; every other role is bound by the package manifest and cannot silently become canonical.

Every governed file f in package P, including P's package.json manifest, has exactly one declared surface role from canonical-instance, declared-component, generated-projection, evidence, fixture, or transient-state. The manifest self-entry is a canonical instance of Canonical Package Manifest/v1. Every canonical instance resolves to exactly one admitted Artifact Type; every other role cannot silently become canonical.

An Artifact Type is a versioned contract T for one artifact kind. T binds at least one semantic Definition, a closed machine schema, canonical-source direction, deterministic human projection, validation rules, owner route, lifecycle posture, and claim ceiling. Registration of T neither defines its subject meaning nor admits T or any instance.

An Artifact Type Registry R is a canonical reference index over immutable Artifact Type contracts and lifecycle-decision overlays. Each entry binds one type version to its exact artifact, schema, discriminator, semantic definitions, lifecycle state, and decision evidence. R references but does not redefine or admit its entries.

An Artifact Type Request Q is a candidate-only intake record created only after resolve_R(a) is empty and compatibility analysis rejects exact reuse. Q describes intended semantics, owner, package home, representation direction, validation purpose, and proposed dependencies, but Q is not a, not an Artifact Type, and has no authority effect.

An Artifact Type Request Q is a candidate-only intake record created only after resolve_R(a) is unresolved and compatibility analysis rejects exact reuse. Q describes intended semantics, owner, package home, representation direction, validation purpose, proposed discriminator, and dependencies. Q is neither subject artifact a nor Artifact Type T, cannot satisfy a subject dependency, and has no authority effect.

Artifact Type Resolution is the deterministic partial function resolve_R(a) that returns exactly one admitted type t when artifact a carries an explicit type reference or one registry-declared discriminator matching t. Zero or multiple admitted matches fail closed; paths, filenames, and labels are not resolution evidence.

Artifact Type Resolution is an executable deterministic operation resolve_R(a) over one canonical machine carrier and one exact registry. An explicit exact reference may select an admitted-current or admitted-historical type; discriminator-only evidence selects admitted-current types. The operation returns resolved for exactly one match, unresolved for zero, and ambiguous for multiple distinct matches. Paths, filenames, extensions, and nearest-name similarity are excluded evidence.

Authority is the normalized definition identified by semantic.authority, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.definition. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D34 without silently merging it with another target.

Target-specific normative meaning:

Authority is an owner-qualified and scope-bounded right or responsibility to decide what a declared term, rule, status, artifact, relation, result, or mutation is permitted to count as for one purpose.

Bound source-semantic basis:

Authority is the scoped right or responsibility to let a term, rule, status,
artifact, relation, gate result, validation result, or mutation count for a
declared CyberAlchemy v2 purpose.

An authority claim is valid only when it names the scope, owner or owner route,
authority surface, governed object, allowed operation, evidence or decision
basis, effect, and challenge or drift route. Authority may decide what counts
inside its scope, but it does not automatically transfer across scopes,
surfaces, owners, generated mirrors, or source spaces.

An Authority Boundary is the explicit owner-scoped limit within which one role may make Governance Decisions about named meanings, targets, and effects. It binds an owner role, an accountable principal binding, an authority scope, allowed effects, excluded effects, and a challenge route. An Authority Boundary is independent of where a workflow requests a decision, and no workflow profile or user preference may create, move, merge, or widen it.

Authority Claim is the normalized definition identified by semantic.authority-claim, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.definition. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D34 without silently merging it with another target.

Target-specific normative meaning:

An Authority Claim is an explicit, challengeable assertion that a named owner or owner route may perform a named operation over a named governed object within an exact scope, on a stated decision or evidence basis, with a declared effect.

Bound source-semantic basis:

Authority is the scoped right or responsibility to let a term, rule, status,
artifact, relation, gate result, validation result, or mutation count for a
declared CyberAlchemy v2 purpose.

An authority claim is valid only when it names the scope, owner or owner route,
authority surface, governed object, allowed operation, evidence or decision
basis, effect, and challenge or drift route. Authority may decide what counts
inside its scope, but it does not automatically transfer across scopes,
surfaces, owners, generated mirrors, or source spaces.

Authority Model is the normalized definition identified by semantic.authority-model, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.definition. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D41 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

An authority model is the governed structure that classifies candidate material by
authority kind, reliance posture, owner route, admissible movement, gate
vocabulary, validation surface, and non-collapse rule so CyberAlchemy v2 can
decide what may count for which purpose without letting evidence, ontology,
research, generated projections, implementation success, or narrative repetition
silently become authority.

An authority model must name the authority surfaces it coordinates, the route
that owns each kind of promotion, the states or postures a candidate may occupy,
the gates that control movement between states, and the boundary conditions that
prevent one authority layer from overriding another.

Authority Promotion is the normalized definition identified by semantic.authority-promotion, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.definition. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D48 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

Authority promotion lifecycle is the single staged path by which any
authority-bearing candidate may acquire authority — `source evidence -> candidate
-> owner-routed review -> promoted authority -> (optional) invariant/constitution
pressure` — with per-stage gates, an owner route, and a stopping/demotion rule. It
is the generalization that `../promotion-policy.md`'s ladder instantiates and that
`CAV2-D43` (patterns), `CAV2-D46` (experience), and the Arcanum Discipline Growth
Rule (disciplines) are instances of.

When an authority-bearing candidate originates in a domain and is proposed as
reusable CAV2 authority, the minimum generalization path is:

```text
domain-owned source or candidate
  -> originating-domain exercise and evidence
  -> CAV2 import candidate
  -> generalized proposal with changes and residue stated
  -> exercise in another independently owned domain or materially distinct context
  -> challenge and contrary-evidence review
  -> CAV2 owner decision
  -> promoted, versioned CAV2 authority
  -> separate adoption by each domain that chooses to use that version
```

This branch applies to domain-originated definitions, rules, methods,
specifications, knowledge structures, validators, and patterns proposed for
CAV2-wide reuse only through an existing authority kind and its owner route.
Proof objects, Lean results, Cedar or Datalog results, tests, observations, and
receipts may support such a candidate as evidence; they do not self-promote.

Authority Surface is the normalized definition identified by semantic.authority-surface, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.definition. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D3 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

An authority layer is a project-local surface that is allowed to define
normative meaning, structural rules, promotion decisions, or contracts for a
specific scope.

Axiom is the normalized definition identified by semantic.axiom, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.definition. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D53 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

An axiom is a **foundational proposition taken as given** — bedrock the system does
not derive further within itself and holds as true (high commitment/veracity) —
**from which a family of premises, invariants, and constitution rules derives**,
such that revising it forces rethinking everything built on it. Its defining
subject is the **world or domain** the system operates in: an axiom states *why*
the system is shaped as it is, and the system is **built around** it rather than
made to satisfy it. It is **not** a constraint on the system's own behavior — that
is an invariant (`CAV2-D54`).

A Bounded Context is a versioned, owner-scoped semantic boundary inside which one declared domain model and one Ubiquitous Language are intended to remain internally consistent for an explicit scope and set of exclusions. Relationships to other Bounded Contexts exist only through separately owned directional Context Maps and contracts.

A Bounded Context is a versioned, owner-scoped semantic boundary inside which one declared domain model and one Ubiquitous Language are intended to remain internally consistent for an explicit scope and set of exclusions. It owns its identity, model, language, scope, contracts, semantic owner, lifecycle, evidence, and challenge route. A Bounded Context does not canonically own map membership or backreferences to Context Maps. Cross-context endpoint membership and directional relationships are owned only by separately governed Context Maps; reverse membership for a context is a generated projection derived from those maps.

Bounded Self-Application Invariant is the normalized invariant identified by semantic.bounded-self-application-invariant, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.invariant. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D30 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

Bounded recursive self-application is the CyberAlchemy v2 invariant that a
governed process may be applied to artifacts produced by that same process only
when each recursive step declares its artifact, altitude or layer, scope, owner,
gate, carried state or residue, recomposition path, and stopping condition.

The recursive move must preserve authority boundaries: the process, the artifact
being processed, the owner route, and the resulting authority posture must remain
distinct unless an explicit promotion or coupling records otherwise.

A Canonical Package Home is the unique governed artifact tree H selected for an owner-local aggregate A by an explicit lifecycle-owner binding and unit-of-change declaration. H carries A's canonical machine sources. Capability, bounded-context, product, DomainSpec, implementation, evidence, and projection facets may be colocated in H when they share A's lifecycle, but their identities and authorities remain distinct and are connected by explicit typed relations. Indexes and global views may reference or generate projections of H; they must not duplicate its canonical carriers.

A Canonical Package Manifest M is the machine-canonical declaration of CPH(A)=H. M names aggregate A, lifecycle owner, unit of change, root H, each governed file role, explicit canonical carriers, and any nested package home with its independent lifecycle and typed parent relation. M describes cohesion but grants no semantic or operational authority.

A Canonical Package Manifest M declares one canonical package home, aggregate, lifecycle owner, unit of change, every governed member's unique surface role, and every independent nested package relation. M must classify its own package.json exactly once as a canonical instance of Canonical Package Manifest/v1. Membership and nesting are explicit data, not directory inference.

Canonical Representation Invariant is the normalized invariant identified by semantic.canonical-representation-invariant, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.invariant. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D51 without silently merging it with another target.

Target-specific normative meaning:

Canonical Representation Invariant requires each artifact to have exactly one declared machine-canonical representation; human views and convenience labels are generated projections, directory placement cannot establish type or authority, and every admitted canonical kind must bind an owner-approved process origin with an honest assurance level.

Bound source-semantic basis:

A canonical artifact is an artifact instance whose **kind is a member of the
canonical-kind enumeration** ([../../ontology/canonical-kinds/CANONICAL-KINDS.md](../../ontology/canonical-kinds/CANONICAL-KINDS.md))
and whose responsible owner has admitted an exact `process_origin` declaration
that names one allowed producer and process for that kind. It therefore carries
a defined type (a `CAV2-D21` classification/schema facet that is bound, not left
as residue) and an owner-declared process origin.

The strength of support for the origin declaration is recorded separately as
`origin_assurance`:

- `declared` means an owner or source made the exact origin statement;
- `integrity-bound` means a verifier confirmed that the statement and bound
  artifact-state bytes match an L1 integrity mechanism; and
- `actor-attested` means an identified actor attested the exact tuple under a
  bound L2 identity policy and external signature.

`actor-attested` is a defined future level, not a currently available result.
No assurance level proves that the named process actually executed, that the
statement is true, or that the artifact is correct or authoritative.

Canonical-ness is therefore the property of *being typed and carrying an
owner-admitted, allowed process-origin declaration with an honest assurance
level*. It is **decoupled from authority** — a canonical artifact may be
non-authoritative and still canonical. An artifact whose kind is not in the
enumeration, or whose exact origin does not resolve to an owner-approved producer
for that kind, is non-canonical or remains blocked as typed residue.

A Capability Instance is an owner-local, version-exact realization or specialization of one Product Capability inside explicitly declared coordination and semantic contexts. It binds separate parent and instance authority lanes, inherited contract, extension scope, adoption decision, D65 construction stages, conformance evidence, lifecycle, drift and recomposition routes, recursion budget or stop, and terminal handoff.

A Capability Realization Binding is a lifecycle-bearing canonical association between one exact Product Capability revision and one or more exact Implementation revisions, with realization role, adoption posture, compatibility, conformance evidence, deployment applicability, owner, succession, and challenge handling. It is neither the Product Capability nor an Implementation and does not prove adoption, deployment, conformance, successful operation, or Product value.

A Challenge Contract is a closed versioned Policy-bound mechanism defining challengeable subjects, eligible challengers, grounds, evidence, response modes, owner route, resolution gate, timing, and unresolved residue handling. A route string alone is not a Challenge Contract, and filing a challenge does not automatically suspend or reverse the subject.

A Challenge Event is an immutable attributable record that an eligible challenger contested one exact subject revision under one exact Challenge Contract with stated grounds and evidence. It is neither the challenged subject, a contradiction finding, resolution, Decision, nor automatic lifecycle transition.

Claim-Support Compatibility Invariant is the normalized invariant identified by semantic.claim-support-compatibility-invariant, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.invariant. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D38 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

Claim <= proof is the CyberAlchemy v2 epistemic invariant that a claim's
asserted strength, authority effect, validation status, or publication posture
must not exceed the proof, evidence, witness, validation result, owner decision,
or accepted premise cited for it.

If support is absent, partial, private, indirect, disputed, or weaker than the
claim, the claim must be downgraded, marked as hypothesis or candidate,
flagged with residue, routed through a gate, or blocked from governing work.

Classification is the governed act and result of assigning an exact subject revision to declared values under independently named axes in one exact Classification Scheme. Classification does not establish identity, Definition meaning, conformance, admission, authority, ownership, causality, realization, success, or ontology truth.

A Classification Assignment is an immutable attributable binding of one exact subject revision to one exact Scheme version, Axis, and Value with basis, evidence, lifecycle, owner, and challenge route. Correction creates a successor assignment; the assignment does not change subject identity or imply facts from other axes.

Classification Axis is the normalized definition identified by semantic.classification-axis, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.definition. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D22 without silently merging it with another target.

Target-specific normative meaning:

A Classification Axis is one explicitly named, independently valued dimension used to classify an artifact or concept for a distinct decision or validation purpose.

Bound source-semantic basis:

Orthogonal classification is the CyberAlchemy v2 rule that a governed
classification axis, taxonomy label, or ontology grouping is admissible only
when it contributes a distinction that is not silently redundant with an
existing axis, label, owner lane, lifecycle state, schema field, or typed
relation.

A classification is orthogonal when changing it does not secretly change a
different authority axis. If a proposed classification cannot stay independent,
its dependency must be represented through `CAV2-D16` typed coupling invariant
before it can govern downstream work.

Classification Orthogonality Invariant is the normalized invariant identified by semantic.classification-orthogonality-invariant, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.invariant. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D22 without silently merging it with another target.

Target-specific normative meaning:

Classification Orthogonality Invariant requires every canonical classification axis to carry a distinct decision or validation purpose; one axis must not be silently inferred from another, redundant canonical labels must be rejected, dependent classifications must be explicit relations, and convenience labels must remain generated projections.

Bound source-semantic basis:

Orthogonal classification is the CyberAlchemy v2 rule that a governed
classification axis, taxonomy label, or ontology grouping is admissible only
when it contributes a distinction that is not silently redundant with an
existing axis, label, owner lane, lifecycle state, schema field, or typed
relation.

A classification is orthogonal when changing it does not secretly change a
different authority axis. If a proposed classification cannot stay independent,
its dependency must be represented through `CAV2-D16` typed coupling invariant
before it can govern downstream work.

A Classification Scheme is a versioned governed contract of axes, allowed values, definitions, cardinality, applicability, exclusions, assignment and evidence rules, hierarchy, mappings, compatibility, owner, and challenge route. A new Scheme version does not silently reinterpret or reclassify assignments made under an older version.

A Classification Value is one governed allowed answer under one exact Classification Axis and Scheme version, with stable identity, meaning, applicability, exclusions, and mappings. Its label is not its identity, and similar labels across axes do not collapse their meanings.

Closed Authority-Kind Invariant is the normalized invariant identified by semantic.closed-authority-kind-invariant, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.invariant. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D49 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

Closed authority-kind enumeration is the invariant that the set of authority
**kinds** is a closed enumeration (the `../AUTHORITY-MODEL.md` Authority Kinds
table). An artifact whose kind is **not** in that enumeration may not acquire or
exercise authority — it defaults to **blocked** pending an owner decision that adds
the kind to the enumeration with its declared lifecycle (`CAV2-D48`) and owner
route. Adding a kind is itself owner-gated.

A Communication Preference is a scoped expression preference for presentation, language, detail, ordering, or interaction style, with source, audience, target, conditions, strength, expiry, and override rules. It is distinct from current instruction, User Decision Preference, Policy, Operational Lesson, and authority.

Conformance is a relation among an exact subject S, exact contract C, declared scope Q, applicable profile P, current evidence set E, and assessment owner. It may be asserted only when P declares E sufficient for every obligation in Q. Different conformance scopes remain orthogonal and cannot be inferred from one another.

Constitution is the normalized definition identified by semantic.constitution, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.definition. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D58 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

A constitution is an **owner-scoped, selector-bound, composable authority
artifact** that turns axioms and invariants into reusable governance rules and
policies for named kinds of governed subject. Those subjects may be artifacts,
tasks or workflows, repository-owned agent actions, system operations or state
transitions, validation surfaces, or authority movements.

A constitution must declare its scope, subject kinds, selectors, owner route,
authority level, rules and policies, precedence and composition behavior,
validation modes or bindings, downstream effect, challenge route, and retirement
or split conditions. It constrains a subject only after an owner decision adopts
the exact constitution version and scope and the subject matches its selectors.
A candidate, selected, or context-loaded constitution does not govern by those
facts alone.

Constraint-Cycle Safety Invariant is the normalized invariant identified by semantic.constraint-cycle-safety-invariant, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.invariant. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D28 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

A value-cycle edge guard is the CyberAlchemy v2 invariant that no relation,
edge type, or ontology movement may simultaneously:

- constrain the value, label, authority state, schema field, or validation
  outcome of another artifact; and
- be allowed to participate in a cycle without an explicit acyclicity
  constraint.

If a proposed relation needs both properties, it must stop at schema governance
and receive a contextuality-obstruction review before it can influence
authority, ontology, validation, or implementation.

Contestability Policy is the normalized policy identified by semantic.contestability-policy, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.policy. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D40 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

A challenge contract is the explicit review surface attached to a
CyberAlchemy v2 node, candidate, claim, or authority artifact that states how
the object may be challenged, contradicted, validated, blocked, or routed for
owner review without silently changing its meaning or confidence.

A challenge contract must declare the valid challenge response, admissible
challenge modes, contradiction and validation links when present, owner route,
resolution gate, blocking questions, and challenge residue route. It does not
contain the object's own confidence or residue and does not introduce a third
confidence axis. Object confidence remains a sibling posture using the
`evidence_confidence` and `commitment_confidence` split governed by `CAV2-D23`.

Context is the normalized definition identified by semantic.context, owned within scope.context-resolution, and carried by type.definition. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D66 without silently merging it with another target.

Target-specific normative meaning:

A Context is a durable, identity-bearing, owner-qualified boundary of relevance and interpretation for one declared purpose, anchored to exactly one Product and, when applicable, one Project and one Goal, with explicit consumers, subject scope, and source policies.

Bound source-semantic basis:

A Context is a durable, identity-bearing, owner-qualified boundary of relevance
and interpretation for one declared purpose. It names the Product, optional
Project, optional Goal, intended consumers and uses, subject scope, and source
policies that frame what information and meaning may be assembled for the work.

Every CyberAlchemy Context belongs to exactly one Product. A project Context
belongs to exactly one Project. A goal Context belongs to exactly one Project
and focuses on exactly one Goal that already belongs to that Project. The first
contract intentionally allows only one primary Goal per Context; cross-goal
work requires separate Contexts or a later explicitly defined composite model.

A Context identity remains stable across new source epochs, resolution
requests, immutable views, interface presentations, session pauses, and
refreshes that preserve its Product, Project, Goal, and purpose. A material
change to any of those anchors creates a successor Context and supersedes the
earlier one instead of silently changing what the earlier identity meant.

A Context Lineage Record is an immutable, owner-qualified statement relating exact predecessor and successor context identities through one typed lineage disposition, with source and destination versions, preserved and changed semantic scopes, decision evidence, effective boundary, challenges, and residue. It records identity history without inferring semantic equivalence or admission.

A Context Map is a versioned, owner-approved set of typed directional relationships between exact Bounded Context versions. Each relationship declares upstream and downstream roles, integration or translation contracts, information and authority limits, owners, evidence, drift handling, and change coordination.

preserving one explicit chain through context, definitions, product and business

construction, independent conformance, bounded operation, recovery, evolution,

records contexts, candidate definitions, blockers, enablers, decisions, gaps,
artifacts, next moves, validation evidence, residue, and recomposition
obligations. Ledgering is the method's continuity mechanism; it is not the whole
method.

In CyberAlchemy v2, Craft method is valid only when it preserves these
boundaries:

- a Product and its Product Thesis own product purpose and value propositions
- a Project coordinates the goals, owners, evidence, decisions, and work used to

A Decision is an attributable authority act that selects an outcome, interpretation, permission, priority, or lifecycle effect for exact subjects within a declared scope and evidence basis. A Decision is distinct from evidence, recommendation, preference, Agent output, execution, and proof that the selected effect occurred.

Every member retains an independent decision identity, Authority Boundary, owner role, accountable principal, immutable target, digest when bytes exist, requested effect, scope, outcome, and invalidation conditions. A Definition is a versioned, owner-scoped semantic artifact that assigns a term one normative meaning within an exact authority scope. Only an exact owner promotion decision can make one exact Definition version canonical authority.

A Delegation is an explicit scope-bounded and time-bounded authorization from a Principal or authority owner to an Agent or Agent Instance for named action kinds under exact Policies, gates, evidence, revocation, and claim ceilings. Delegation transfers neither identity nor ownership and creates no authority outside its exact envelope.

A Derived Refresh is the deterministic regeneration and validation of a noncanonical projection from an unchanged canonical machine input under an exact generator binding. It records the canonical input digest, generator identity and digest, output digest, parity result, and validation receipt. A Derived Refresh creates no Semantic Epoch, Representation Revision, Governance Decision, or authority effect. A change to the generator is governed separately as a tooling change even when refreshing its outputs has no semantic effect.

Discipline is the normalized definition identified by semantic.discipline, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.definition. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D50 without silently merging it with another target.

A Drift Assessment is an evidence-bounded comparison between declared and observed versions, conditions, bindings, meanings, behavior, or currentness at an exact time. Mismatch does not by itself establish cause, severity, failure, correction authority, or required remediation.

An Effect is a declared change in governed state, rights, obligations, external condition, or interpretation that a Decision or Action intends, authorizes, records, or observes under an exact effect kind. Declaring, authorizing, attempting, delivering, and observing an Effect are separate facts.

Research is a bounded, attributable investigation that gathers and organizes

Exact Publication Authorization Invariant is the normalized invariant identified by semantic.exact-publication-authorization-invariant, owned within scope.repository-governance, and carried by type.invariant. Exact publication authorization is the CyberAlchemy v2 rule that private
material may cross a publication boundary only after two separate decisions:

1. every source owner authorizes an exact candidate slice, its allowed claims,
   audience, channel, privacy policies, and requested publishing principal; and
2. after private generation and privacy validation, that publishing principal
   approves the exact final output bytes, digest, audience, channel, and claim
   ceiling.

The first decision permits creation and review of a private publication
candidate. It does not permit unknown future bytes to be published. The second
decision applies only to the exact output it binds. Any change to the sources,
claims, policies, generator, output bytes, audience, channel, or publishing
principal requires the applicable decisions to be repeated.

All material is private by default when no valid exact authorization exists.
Generation, validation, proof, obligation discharge, CAV2 promotion, or domain
adoption does not grant publication permission.

Experience evidence lifecycle is the CyberAlchemy v2 lifecycle by which an

The normal path is:

```text
interface observation or UI hypothesis

  -> lesson
  -> ux-pattern candidate

  -> fixture, browser, or cross-session exercise
  -> challenge and residue review

```

An interface pattern is not authoritative because it looked better once. It must
carry evidence and survive the claim class appropriate to its evidence.

Four-facet action method is the CyberAlchemy v2 primitive action rule that every
governed action must explicitly bind, create, or record typed residue for four
facets before the action can govern downstream work:

- classification or taxonomy facet
- schema facet
- human-continuation view
- machine-checkable view

A governed action is any CyberAlchemy v2 action that creates, changes, routes,
validates, promotes, implements, or interprets load-bearing artifacts, state,
meaning, or authority posture. The action is admissible only when each facet is
declared or when its absence is carried as typed residue.

At minimum:

- the classification or taxonomy facet states what kind of thing or action is
  involved and which classification catalog, taxonomy, or source vocabulary owns
  that assignment
- the schema facet states the structural shape, field set, relation shape, or
  validation surface that governs the action or artifact
- the human-continuation view states how a human can understand the action's
  purpose, status, trust boundary, blockers, residue, next route, and evidence
- the machine-checkable view states how a machine can parse or check the action
  state, including identifiers, kind, schema reference, classification
  reference, source of truth, validator or proof handle, projection status, and
  residue

If a facet is missing, impossible, or intentionally deferred, the action must
record typed residue naming the missing facet, the reason or impossibility, the
owner route, the evidence reference, and the action effect: continue, defer, or
block. If the action later asks to promote something, the same residue must also
state the promotion effect.

A gate is an explicit checkpoint that decides or routes whether a candidate

Every CyberAlchemy v2 gate must declare its owner route, scope, inputs,

It does not embed Implementation in Intent, prove delivery or satisfaction, or authorize unrelated work.

Interface Claim-Support Compatibility Invariant is the normalized invariant identified by semantic.interface-claim-support-compatibility-invariant, owned within scope.ux-ui, and carried by type.invariant. Interface evidence boundary is the CyberAlchemy v2 rule that UX/UI claims must
state which kind of evidence can support them and what that evidence cannot
prove.

At minimum, UX/UI claims must be classified as one of:

- hard gate
- soft flag
- screenshot review
- human study
- not automatable

Browser automation may directly support page-load, accessibility-tree,
keyboard, layout, interaction, screenshot, trace, console/network, and DOM
measurement claims. It may prepare evidence for cognitive, attention,
perception, trust, comprehension, delight, and real-user success claims, but it
must not turn them into deterministic authority without calibrated fixtures and
owner approval.

Invariant is the normalized definition identified by semantic.invariant, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.definition. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D54 without silently merging it with another target.

An invariant is a **condition on the system's own behavior or artifacts that must
remain true** across a declared scope of decisions, transformations, or states —
such that a violation is **drift or a defect**. Its defining subject is the
**system**: unlike an axiom (`CAV2-D53`), which the system is built around, an
invariant is something the system **must satisfy** and can fail to. An invariant is
the checkable *what-must-stay-true* that a constitution rule (`CAV2-D58`)
operationalizes and a validator or gate (`CAV2-D37`) enforces.

A Ledger is a governed ordered collection of independently identifiable entries maintained under an exact entry schema, ordering rule, integrity rule, correction policy, reconciliation procedure, owner, lifecycle, retention, and challenge contract. Ledger does not imply append-only storage, event sourcing, accounting, truth, evidence acceptance, Decision authority, or one universal Ledger Artifact Type.

A Lesson Application is an immutable record that one exact Operational Lesson revision was selected and actually used or deliberately not used for one later Session or Action. Selection, presentation, applicability, use, compliance, and success are separate facts.

A Lesson Outcome Assessment is an evidence-bounded comparison of one Lesson Application’s predicted benefit or falsifier with its observed outcome. Task completion, repetition, Agent self-report, or absence of correction alone does not prove benefit.

A schema is an explicit declaration of **admissible structure**. It names four
things:

- **kinds** — the sorts of thing that may occur;
- **constraints** — what may occupy a kind: a decidable predicate over a *single*
  occupant's structure;
- **relations** — the connections that may hold *between* kinds;
- **connection rules** — how those relations may be formed: which kinds they may
  connect, with what multiplicity, and which composite paths must agree.

Constraints and connection rules are **separate parts and do not reduce to one
another**: a constraint on allowed values says nothing about how two kinds may
relate, and a rule on relating says nothing about what may fill a slot.

A schema is stated **independently of any particular occupant**, so that
conformance is decidable **by inspection alone** — without executing the thing,
populating it, or interpreting what it means. Conformance is therefore **shape
evidence**, and never by itself authority: a schema-valid artifact has proved its
form, not its truth, its ownership, or its promotion.

A Team is a durable, owner-qualified collective identity through which Persons coordinate toward one declared purpose and scope, independently of its changing memberships, roles, responsibilities, and authority relations.

Bound source-semantic basis:

A Team is a durable, owner-qualified collective identity through which Persons
coordinate toward one declared purpose and scope. Its identity, lifecycle,
membership, roles, responsibilities, and authority relationships are explicit
and remain separate.

A Team is not merely the current set of its members. Membership changes do not
silently create a different Team while its identity, purpose, scope, and owner
boundary remain stable. An active Team has at least one current Person
membership. A proposed Team may exist before its first membership so its
purpose and owner can be reviewed without inventing members.

A Tool is a governed invocable resource used by an Agent Action through a declared interface, version, input/output contract, failure boundary, and evidence route. Tool availability grants neither Agent Capability nor authority and does not prove correct invocation or effect.

Traceability is the normalized definition identified by semantic.traceability, owned within scope.lineage, and carried by type.definition. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D36 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

Traceability is the ability to follow explicit, typed links across intent,
source evidence, provenance, definitions, rules, methods, artifacts, gates,
validation, decisions, residue, and next routes so that a later human or agent
can answer why something exists, what it depends on, what it affects, and where
to continue.

Traceability is satisfied only when the relevant chain has enough link targets,
relation types, authority postures, and residue markers to be traversed without
hidden conversation context.

The Typed Connection Extension Rule requires every global Relation Kind to expose a finite closed set of exact ordered source-kind to target-kind connections. A proposed extension must bind one effective predecessor Relation Kind version, one source endpoint contract, one target endpoint contract, direction, global scope, an exact qualifier schema with pair-specific values and constraints, canonical relation authority, contestability, owner, evidence, lifecycle effect, validation effect, and the exact successor contract version. It may reuse the Relation Kind only when the same unique semantic question remains intact; otherwise it must propose a distinct Relation Kind. Ontology-local connections must remain scoped to their exact Ontology contract. No global connection is created by endpoint registration, separate source and target lists, wildcard matching, historical observation, local graph use, shared naming, candidate validation, endpoint admission, or a second writable projection.

Typed Coupling Invariant is the normalized invariant identified by semantic.typed-coupling-invariant, owned within scope.shared-authority, and carried by type.invariant. Any canonical instance must preserve that classification and the accepted source relations to CAV2-D16 without silently merging it with another target.

Bound source-semantic basis:

A typed coupling invariant is the CyberAlchemy v2 rule that any dependency,
bridge, constraint, influence, or co-change relation between non-orthogonal
artifacts, concepts, stages, authorities, or owners must be represented as an
explicit typed relation with named endpoints, direction, relation kind, owner,
evidence, and validation or promotion effect.

A Typed Relation is one independently identified global connection between exact source and target instances under one admitted Relation Kind version, exact allowed pair, qualifiers, owner, evidence, lifecycle, and contestability contract. It neither merges endpoint identities nor becomes valid from schema fields, shared paths, Ontology projection, or candidate validation.

A Ubiquitous Language is the owner-governed set of expressions, concepts, relations, interpretation rules, usage surfaces, ambiguities, and revision routes used to express one Bounded Context's model. Each load-bearing expression resolves to one current concept disposition within that context or remains explicitly unresolved.

A User Decision Preference is a versioned user-owned interaction configuration that selects one preferred Decision Checkpoint for an exact workflow type or workflow instance scope. It is applied only when the selected checkpoint is allowed by the applicable Workflow Decision Profile. An invalid preference blocks resolution and must not silently fall back. A preference has no authority effect and cannot waive a required decision, create standing authority, or alter an owner, target, effect, or scope.

Validation is an Evaluation V of exact subject S against exact criteria profile P. V produces check outcomes and a receipt. A PASS establishes only that every evaluable criterion declared by P passed for the bound inputs; it becomes conformance evidence only when an applicable conformance profile declares those checks sufficient for an exact scope.

A Validation Receipt is an immutable record R of one validation event. R binds exact identities and digests for the subject, criteria profile, validator, inputs, environment, complete outcomes, evidence, causal blockers, and claim ceiling. Recording R preserves traceability but cannot change the subject's authority or lifecycle by itself.

A Withdrawal Record is a permanent governance and lineage record that reserves one retired or rejected identifier, binds the exact withdrawn subject and digest when available, states the reason and effective time, names any successor authority, preserves evidence and owner decision, and exposes a challenge route. It does not delete history, erase prior references, reuse the identifier, imply a successor exists, or automatically supersede another subject.

Work is a bounded unit of coordinated effort with a declared purpose, owner, participants, inputs, expected result, constraints, lifecycle, and outcome trace. Work is not necessarily a Project and does not imply authority, completion, successful outcome, or Product value.

A Work Outcome Assessment is an evidence-bounded comparison between one Work item or Agent Action’s declared expected result and its observed result. It does not by itself establish lesson value, causal attribution, Product value, acceptance, or authority effect.

Target-specific normative meaning:

Work-State Continuity Capability is the ability to preserve and reconstruct current work state across people, agents, sessions, interruptions, and child contexts from one declared ledger containing decisions, blockers, evidence, artifacts, residue, and next routes.

Bound source-semantic basis:

A Craft execution surface is the project-local Craft ledger, derived index, and
linked human view used to record recursive work state, blockers, decisions,
candidate definitions, gaps, artifacts, next moves, and recomposition evidence
for a bounded project scope.

Craft method is CyberAlchemy's governed recursive system-building method. It
turns owner-controlled Product intent into an evidence-bounded working system by
preserving one explicit chain through context, definitions, product and business
meaning, system specification, exact realization selection, deterministic
construction, independent conformance, bounded operation, recovery, evolution,
and owner continuation.

The method uses a source-of-truth ledger to preserve state across that chain. It
records contexts, candidate definitions, blockers, enablers, decisions, gaps,
artifacts, next moves, validation evidence, residue, and recomposition
obligations. Ledgering is the method's continuity mechanism; it is not the whole
method.

In CyberAlchemy v2, Craft method is valid only when it preserves these
boundaries:

- a Product and its Product Thesis own product purpose and value propositions
- a Project coordinates the goals, owners, evidence, decisions, and work used to
  develop or evolve the Product
- Product Features and Product Capabilities remain distinct from the Product,
  Project, Method, and their realizations
- canonical definitions, product and business ontology, DomainSpec source,
  generated system ontology, realization selection, construction, conformance,
  runtime evidence, and owner decisions remain separately identifiable
- every implementation-bearing construction follows the exact
  `CAV2-D65` DomainSpec-governed construction chain or carries typed residue for
  the missing prerequisite
- `.craft/ledger.yml` or an equivalent declared ledger is the source of truth
  for Craft state
- `CRAFT.md`, `.craft/index.json`, projections, and status output are derived
  views
- residue is typed and carried forward instead of hidden
- schema-level and instance-level validation are not collapsed
- child contexts recompose into their parent through evidence
- closure happens by owner decision, gate, or accepted residue, not by a claim
  of total final completion
- Craft state can carry local candidate definitions and receipts but cannot
  make terms canonical without definitions-governance

A Workflow Decision Profile is a versioned configuration owned by one workflow type that declares decision_mode as none or single, the allowed Decision Checkpoints, an optional explicit default, required decision-target availability, standing-authority requirements for none mode, invalidation conditions, and post-decision continuation limits. It constrains checkpoint resolution but never performs a Governance Decision or grants authority.

A Decision Checkpoint is one Workflow-local position at which a closed Decision Request Set may be presented as one human interaction. It carries no authority. Its placement is resolved from the applicable Workflow Decision Profile and User Decision Preference, while every request retains its independently governed owner, scope, exact target, and effect.

A Decision Request Set is a closed ordered set of exact decision requests presented at one Decision Checkpoint. Every member retains its independent decision identity, authority scope, owner, target, digest when bytes exist, requested effect, outcome, and invalidation conditions. Presentation reduces interaction count but cannot merge authority, infer authorization between members, or let one outcome satisfy another gate.

A User Decision Preference is a versioned user-owned interaction configuration selecting one preferred Decision Checkpoint for an exact Workflow type or instance scope. It applies only when allowed by the Workflow Decision Profile. An explicit invalid preference blocks resolution and never silently falls back. A preference has no authority effect and cannot waive a required decision, create standing authority, or alter an owner, target, effect, or scope.

A Workflow Decision Profile is a versioned configuration owned by one Workflow type. It declares decision_mode as none or single, its allowed Decision Checkpoints, an optional explicit default, target-availability requirements, standing-authority requirements for none mode, invalidation conditions, and post-decision continuation limits. It constrains interaction resolution but does not perform a decision or grant authority.
